summary: Defines an extension to the Management Information Base for managing the frame relay service in TCP/IP-based networks.

eli5.summary: Frame relay is a way phone companies carry data. This gives tools a way to watch and manage it.

questions: how to manage frame relay with snmp
what is the frame relay service mib
how to manage frame relay pvcs with snmp
subtitle: An SNMP MIB that lets a customer monitor a carrier's frame relay service: ports, PVCs, counters and alarms.

tldr.problem: Customers of a frame relay network service had no standard way to see the configuration, performance and faults of the interfaces and virtual circuits they were buying.
tldr.mechanism: The Frame Relay Service MIB models a customer's logical ports, signaling, PVC end-points, PVC connections, accounting and status notifications as SNMP objects, served by a single virtual Frame Relay Service agent.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2954 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 1604 and is updated by RFC 9141. It adds optional read-write objects, fragmentation control, FR/ATM interworking and extra frame counters.

today: RFC 2954 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 1604 and is updated by RFC 9141, so read that update alongside it.

sections.title: Scope and the Service Agent
sections.content:
This memo defines a Management Information Base (MIB) module for managing a frame relay service. It supports Customer Network Management: through this and related MIBs, a customer's management station can monitor its UNI/NNI logical ports and PVCs, and get configuration data, performance information and fault detection. Optionally, an agent may let the customer create, delete, modify, activate and deactivate individual PVCs.

The MIB models every interface and PVC delivered by the service inside one virtual SNMP system, even if they physically sit on several devices. An SNMP agent that supports it is called a Frame Relay Service (FRS) agent. Internal switching elements, line cards and routing tables are out of scope, and so is the physical layer.

The customer's management station will typically reach the agent over a frame relay PVC, using SNMP over UDP over IP encapsulated in frame relay. The MIB is not implemented on user equipment (DTE), which is managed with the Frame Relay DTE MIB (RFC 2115). It supports PVCs, and may be extended later to cover SVCs.

Two compliance modules separate the roles: frnetservCompliance for the read-only service view and frnetSwitchCompliance for switch management, which includes administrative control objects.
sections.eli5: The phone company runs the network, but you get a window into your own part of it. You can look through the window, and sometimes adjust things, but you cannot see how the machines inside work.

sections.title: Terms and Multi-Network PVCs
sections.content:
The RFC defines the vocabulary it uses. An access channel is the pathway for a single stream of user data on a DS1/E1 or DS3/E3 line. CIR, the Committed Information Rate, is the data rate the network commits to deliver under normal conditions, averaged over a time interval Tc (CIR = Bc/Tc). Bc is the committed burst size and Be the excess burst size delivered with lower probability. A PVC is a virtual connection whose end-points and bearer capabilities are defined at subscription time, and a logical port models the frame relay interface on a device.

The MIB manages only one provider's service. If a customer PVC crosses several networks, the customer must poll a different FRS agent in each network to get the end-to-end view. Each part of the PVC inside one network is a PVC segment.

Because many subscribers share the network, each should see only its own interfaces and PVCs, so the FRS agent should offer instance-level granularity for MIB views.
sections.eli5: If your delivery route passes through three companies, you have to call each one to find out how your parcel is doing. Each company only tells you about its own stretch.

sections.title: Fitting Into Other MIBs
sections.content:
The MIB applies to interfaces with ifType frameRelayService (44). The RFC says how to fill in the standard System group for the FRS agent and how to interpret the Interfaces table (ifTable, ifXTable) for a frame relay logical port. For example, ifType is 44, ifSpeed is the user information transfer rate (1,536,000 bits per second for a DS1-based port and 1,984,000 for an E1-based port), and ifName is a zero-length string.

Link up and down notifications are enabled at the frame relay service layer, because PVC notifications are not sent if the interface fails and the management station would otherwise never hear about it. The Interface Stack group must be supported, and the RFC gives worked examples of ifStackTable entries for frame relay over DS0s on a DS1 and over a V.35 line.

A connection that spans frame relay and ATM is recorded in the frAtmIwfConnectionTable of the FR/ATM PVC Service Interworking MIB instead of in this MIB's connection table. In that case frPVCEndptConnectIdentifier is set to zero.
sections.eli5: The new dashboard does not replace the standard one. It plugs into it, and the document explains which dial on the standard dashboard means what for frame relay.

sections.title: Ports, Signaling and Link Management
sections.content:
The module is rooted under transmission 44. Its first table, frLportTable, adds frame relay facts to each interface: the numbering plan (E.164, X.121 or none), contact and location, whether the port is a UNI or an NNI, the Q.922 address and DLCI length, and the signaling protocol in use (none, LMI, ANSI T1.617 Annex D or B, or ITU Q.933 Annex A).

Some objects are read-write: frLportTypeAdmin and frLportVCSigProtocolAdmin set the desired port type and signaling protocol, and frLportFragControl and frLportFragSize control FRF.12 fragmentation. frLportDLCIIndexValue gives a hint for the next free DLCI index to use when creating a PVC end-point.

The frMgtVCSigTable exposes the local in-channel signaling parameters (the N391, N392, N393 and T391 style counters and timers, with defaults such as 6, 3, 4 and 10 on the user side) and error counters, together with Admin variants for setting them. The older frLportVCSigPointer object is deprecated because all signaling parameters now live in this single table.
sections.eli5: Each connection point to the network has a little profile card: what kind of point it is, how it checks the line is alive, and how often. Some cards can be edited by the manager.

sections.title: PVC End-Points and Connections
sections.content:
A PVC segment end-point is identified by a logical port index and a DLCI index and lives in frPVCEndptTable. It holds the traffic parameters (maximum frame size, Bc, Be and CIR, separately for the In and Out directions) and many statistics, including frames, octets, discards, discard-eligible frames, and FECN and BECN counts. A unidirectional PVC is modeled with zero traffic parameters in one direction.

The creation procedure has two steps. First, create the end-point rows with their traffic parameters; a point-to-point PVC has two. Second, obtain a unique index from frPVCConnectIndexValue, create rows in frPVCConnectTable with frPVCConnectRowStatus to join the end-points, and set frPVCConnectAdminStatus to active(1) in all rows to turn the PVC on. Not all implementations support creating or changing PVCs over SNMP.

The connect table names the two ends low and high by comparing ifIndex values, so each direction has its own operational status. A unidirectional PVC has one direction down.
sections.eli5: First you describe each end of a pipe and how much it can carry. Then you tell the system which two ends belong together, and turn the pipe on.

sections.title: Accounting, Notifications and Conformance
sections.content:
Accounting tables count traffic in segments. frAccountPVCTable tracks in and out segments per PVC end-point, with a segment size in octets, and frAccountLportTable does the same per logical port.

The notification frPVCConnectStatusNotif says a PVC has changed state and carries the two direction statuses and the received signaling status. It is not sent when a UNI changes state; a link down or link up notification is used instead. The older frPVCConnectStatusChange is deprecated because it wrongly included index values and did not use the trap prefix needed for automatic SMIv2 to SMIv1 conversion.

The remaining pages define compliance modules and object groups, including historical ones for RFC 1604.
sections.eli5: There is a meter that counts how much was used for billing, and an alarm bell that rings when one of your pipes switches on or off.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some objects have read-write or read-create access and may be sensitive in some networks. Allowing SET operations in an unprotected environment can harm network operations. No managed object in the MIB contains sensitive information.

SNMPv1 by itself is not secure, and even a secure network such as one using IPSec does not control who on it may GET or SET these objects. Implementers are recommended to use the SNMPv3 framework, specifically the User-based Security Model (RFC 2574) and the View-based Access Control Model (RFC 2575). Configuring the SNMP entity so only legitimate principals can access the objects is the customer's or user's responsibility.
sections.eli5: If anyone could press the buttons on the dashboard, they could break things. So use the proper locks that come with the newer version of SNMP.
